clue.text: Slander Irishman visiting New York

blocks.note: a man's first name, used here for a Gaelic Irishman
the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: An Irishman on a trip to New York is accused of slandering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' simply puts the man beside the city abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging statement about someone, the same thing as slander.

clue.text: Type of flower produced from a bulb recently out round river

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been knocked into disorder and must be rearranged
the rearranged letters go round the outside of the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A gardener explains that a flower grew from a bulb that was planted out near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like the bulb was planted out, but it signals the jumble; 'round' then wraps the result about the river abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury bell is a campanula, a garden plant with large bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Reason one joins record clubs?

blocks.note: a log is a written record, such as a ship's log
the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Asks why a person would join several record clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joins' places the one between the record and the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, so it serves as a noun synonym for reason.

clue.text: Way of presenting data from MUD? Email it, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters are one possible rearrangement of what follows

blocks.note: all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonders whether data from a MUD, an online multi-user game, could be emailed.
explanation.walkthrough: MUD was an early text-based online game, which makes the computing surface fit the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia presentation combines text, sound, images and video to put across information.

clue.text: Coarse person in hostelry, a hooker

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the next two

explanation.surface: A rough customer is found in a pub alongside a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans hostelrY A HOOker.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo, from the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels, is a crude, uncultivated lout.

clue.text: Property close to Nice, say

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the French city's name
to state is to say

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line about a property near Nice on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads like 'near' but takes the last letter of Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed property, a house with its grounds.

clue.text: Ten operas rewritten in international language

indicators.note: something rewritten is put down again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten operas have been translated into a language everyone could understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the constructed language created in 1887 for use between nations.

clue.text: Instant credit

blocks.note: first meaning: a moment
second meaning: buying on ... means on credit

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a loan approved on the spot; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage gives the word both a moment of time and deferred payment, as in 'buy on tick'.

clue.text: One who's got designs on some of you?

definitions.text: One who's got designs on some of you?

blocks.clueFragment: One who's got designs on some of you?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone with schemes or intentions towards some of the people being addressed
setter's reading: a person who literally puts pictures onto parts of your body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Having designs on' someone idiomatically means plotting against them; here the designs are inked onto skin, and 'some of you' is part of your body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist is an artist who marks permanent designs into a client's skin.

clue.text: Red-hot on box, yet comic is just an ordinary young chap?

indicators.note: comic suggests a playful, absurd treatment, so the letters are jumbled about

blocks.note: all fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV comedian is hot property on the box, yet seems just an ordinary lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is British slang for television, which makes the surface about a comic on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy next door is an idiom for a wholesome, unremarkable young man.

clue.text: Trap about to be laid by the Spanish boy

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for a trap is read the other way

blocks.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A hunter sets a snare and lays it alongside a Spanish lad.
explanation.walkthrough: GIN reversed gives NIG, then EL completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel is a man's first name, so it stands for a boy in cryptic convention.

clue.text: Bound to put an end to children's game

blocks.note: to bound is to leap or hop
to scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to stop children playing their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but Bound is the verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is the playground game of hopping through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Rectories I mixed up delivering desk

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddled vicarages are handing over an item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, often with drawers and a fold-down top.

clue.text: Cat, black, in vault

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A black cat has got shut inside a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests leaping, but here it is the burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault in the burial sense is a tomb, an underground chamber for the dead.

clue.text: Adroit male rolled a cigarette

indicators.note: rolled means turned over and over, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deft man skilfully rolls himself a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a rolled cigarette is the opposite of the answer, which is a ready-made one, as opposed to a roll-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailor-made is informal slang for a manufactured cigarette, contrasted with a hand-rolled one.

clue.text: Stategy to avoid unpleasant realities employed by one in a trap?

definitions.text: employed by one in a trap

blocks.note: first meaning: a defensive, siege-like attitude that shuts out the world

blocks.clueFragment: employed by one in a trap
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: the thinking of someone stuck in a golf course's sand trap

explanation.walkthrough: In golf a bunker is a sand-filled hazard, also called a trap, so the phrase is read literally. 'Stategy' is printed so in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunker mentality is a siege attitude of defensive self-justification that refuses to face criticism or facts.

clue.text: Lots again suffering homesickness

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: all nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people are once more pining for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia originally named homesickness, a longing to return to home or the past.

clue.text: Beggar declaring inability to rehabilitate?

blocks.note: to mend is to repair or restore
what someone says when declaring they are unable

explanation.surface: A beggar claims to be beyond reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as MEND + I CAN'T, someone saying they cannot mend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, especially a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: To play this, must one have a round using an iron?

definitions.text: To play this, must one have a round using an iron?

blocks.clueFragment: have a round using an iron
blocks.note: surface reading: playing a round of golf with an iron club
setter's reading: a single bullet in a gun, 'iron' being slang for a pistol

explanation.walkthrough: Golf words lead astray: a round is also a cartridge and an iron is old slang for a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: In this deadly gamble a revolver loaded with one cartridge is spun and fired at one's own head.

clue.text: Carry last of wine into pub

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the following word
into means that letter is placed inside the next word

blocks.note: the final letter of wine
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Bring the remaining wine into the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: In nightclub, hold forth about duo, initially off-key

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a disco is a nightclub
to rant is to hold forth at length
the opening letter of duo

explanation.surface: A singing pair is out of tune in a nightclub while someone lectures them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies only to duo, and only the holding-forth word goes about that letter; the nightclub stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discordant is harsh and inharmonious, so it is out of tune or off-key.

clue.text: This game teaches strategy, in part

indicators.note: in part says the letters form a portion of the words that come before

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A game whose teaching value lies in strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across teaCHES Strategy, and the whole clue also describes the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game famous for training long-term strategic thinking.

clue.text: Short cut — over 10 minutes, in truth

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to axe is to cut
the digits written as letters I and O
M is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: A short edit has run more than ten minutes over, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means placed on top, so the shortened cut sits above the rest; 10 is read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth accepted without proof.

clue.text: Up endlessly making wine

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: astir means up and about

explanation.surface: Staying up all night producing wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont region of Italy.

clue.text: Member hasn't arrived on time to do what members do?

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
someone who hasn't come on time is late

explanation.surface: A member of parliament turns up late for making laws.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Member' is a body part; the second 'members' are Members of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a parliament pass laws, which is to legislate.

clue.text: Friend, male one, filling in the past

indicators.note: filling in means these pieces are stuffed inside the next word

blocks.note: ago means in the past
M is the abbreviation for male
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A male friend once filled in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: M and I together go inside AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English too.

clue.text: The French deserter carrying one rope

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: la is French for the, feminine form
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French deserter carries off a single rope.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat is slang for a deserter, from rats leaving a sinking ship; it is the deserter, not the whole phrase, that carries the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long rope with a running noose.

clue.text: Pilot goes about a mile in vessel

indicators.note: goes about means wrapping round something, so the outer word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: to pilot a boat is to steer it
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A ship's pilot travels around a mile in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like part of the pilot's story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, a vessel powered by steam engines.
